# R380 — phase refill queue and bandwidth-path audit

Date: 2026-10-13 (Asia/Tokyo). Read-only source/spec review for supplied worktree `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/feat-phase-cache-stock-bench-20261013`, clean HEAD `499f226a0f3b46aa1bdcd0314fd0f81558799f6f`. Only this report was written. No GPU/model/test/build/import/AST/profiler/process/service/Git/cleanup action was performed. The active phaseON measurement and its logs/config were not inspected or changed. Current official phaseON remains not done; no result is inferred from the OFF control.

## Finding

The phase VMM payload path currently does not use a copy-only queue. `PhaseCacheOwner::fill_checked` calls backend `write`, then backend `read`, then exact `memcmp`; `GpuBackend::write/read` both call `gpu::copy`. That helper submits `queue.memcpy` to `Runtime::compute()` and waits synchronously for the event. Therefore every checked fill currently has two serialized blocking copy calls on the default compute queue. The 768-fill diagnostic from R375 measured 1,571,635,200 logical bytes in each direction, with H2D host time 1,441.241 ms and D2H 412.846 ms. This is about 1.09 GB/s H2D and 3.81 GB/s D2H when dividing logical request bytes by those host counters. These are application-requested copy sizes and nested host timing, not measured PCIe/DRAM traffic or direct link-bandwidth measurements. The timing gap R375 calculated remains unassigned; this audit does not attribute it to FNV or logging.

A checked native COPY queue is a technically plausible candidate for these phase copies at the SYCL/API-contract level. The SYCL VMM extension explicitly says a mapped VMM pointer behaves like device USM and can be used in any interface accepting a device USM pointer. SYCL `queue::memcpy` accepts host pointers or device-accessible USM pointers; Level Zero's copy command likewise requires both endpoints to be accessible to the command-list device and in the same context. The mapped phase destination meets the VMM extension's documented device-USM-equivalent contract. The H2D source is host USM from the immutable expert arena (R375); the D2H verification destination is an ordinary `std::vector<uint8_t>` host pointer, which is permitted by the explicit SYCL memcpy contract. This establishes API-level pointer eligibility, not that the exact installed SYCL/UR/driver/native-import combination has been exercised successfully with this VMM mapping and both pointer classes.

`sycl::get_pointer_type` answers whether a pointer lies inside a valid USM allocation; a virtual reservation plus physical VMM mapping is not such an allocation and may query as `unknown`. That query result must not be used to reject the documented VMM pointer from the SYCL copy operation, nor may code infer its runtime/context owner from the query. The queue must instead be selected from the phase cache's known `Runtime`/device/context and passed explicitly. Existing `gpu::copy` has no stream parameter and hardcodes compute, while `gpu::copy_async` already accepts an explicit stream.

## Queue, event, and lifetime seams

- `gpu::copy_stream_create()` calls `Runtime::create_copy_stream()`. With exact `STRATA_COPY_ENGINE=1`, the existing factory on Level Zero checks for a bounded command-queue group with COPY and without COMPUTE, creates an in-order asynchronous immediate command list, imports it as a SYCL queue with `ownership::keep`, and stores the native owner beside the imported queue. Unsupported/pre-import cases fall back to a generic engine stream. Service-event profiling forces generic queue selection. Post-import ambiguity/insertion and checked native teardown have fail-stop/retention handling; preserve these contracts. Copy-only streams refuse compute, graph, and host-task use. The current `STRATA_COPY_ENGINE` branch is therefore not automatically phase routing: current phase code calls `gpu::copy`, and the existing stream-factory call is owned by Prefill's separate copy stream.
- A phase-specific explicit stream handle is the safe routing seam; do not infer queue role from the VMM pointer, operation shape, or a global default. It would need to be created on the phase's exact Runtime/context and have an explicit owner whose lifetime encloses all queued operations. Existing `Runtime::create_copy_stream()` can provide either native or generic behavior under its current selector/fallback rules, but any change to when/how the selector is applied must preserve the service-events exclusion and the copy-only guard.
- A minimal first candidate should keep the current serial checked contract: submit one `copy_async(dst, src, bytes, phase_stream)`, then `stream_sync(phase_stream)` and check both returns before reusing either endpoint. For a native copy-only queue, `Runtime::finish(queue)` waits on an in-order queue barrier using the runtime wait/error check and fail-stops if drain is uncertain. Do not replace checked completion with event polling or assume ordering across the compute and copy queues. The current path waits every copy before proceeding, so the fill/write/read/compare sequence already has explicit completion boundaries; keeping those boundaries avoids introducing cross-queue producer/consumer races.
- `fill_checked` sets `readers_ready_ = false`, requires a mapped vacant slot and correct immutable source geometry, writes, reads back, checks exact equality, and only then stages the slot. Preserve this sequence and the existing owner poison/fail-stop behavior. The source Host-USM block must stay alive through H2D completion; the mapped physical handle and virtual reservation must remain attached through both copies; the ordinary verification vector must not be read/overwritten until D2H completion and `memcmp` is finished. Do not detach/unmap or destroy queue/native owners while completion is unknown. Phase publication and reader retirement remain separate checked boundaries.
- `gpu::copy_async` returns after submission, whereas `gpu::stream_sync` drains the supplied queue; `gpu::copy` is a synchronous compute-queue helper. `gpu::event_record` can put a non-timing barrier on a copy-only stream but rejects timing/profiling tags. Avoid adding an event solely to recover the synchronous semantics for the first candidate. A later batch path would need explicit batch-event ownership and bounded staging/readback lifetimes, and is a different design requiring its own review.

## Minimal source candidate and evidence required

Source-only candidate: give the phase GPU backend an explicitly owned copy stream/queue handle, route each `write`/`read` through `gpu::copy_async` on that handle, and synchronously drain/check it before returning. Initially keep one operation per completion boundary, byte-for-byte readback validation, ordinary vector readback, exact slot state transitions, and current fail-stop policy. Native selection should remain opt-in and use the already checked bounded COPY-only Level Zero factory; unsupported/provider-ineligible cases should select the generic queue before native import. Avoid repurposing the prefill-owned stream implicitly or broadening the native route to other callers. This source candidate is not a claim that the native queue will improve speed, that the hardware has an available idle copy engine, or that current ON benchmark is valid.

Minimal qualification sequence after Main closes its current run: (1) a focused non-model API correctness probe on the exact shipped compiler/SYCL/UR/Level Zero stack: same-context VMM-mapped device destination, host-USM H2D source, ordinary vector D2H destination, both directions over representative sizes, explicit completion and byte equality, plus failure/unknown-completion retention; verify the imported queue really has the expected copy-only properties and cannot submit compute; (2) serialized real phase-fill comparison using same source/profile/slot set, with the generic-compute route as baseline and copy-stream route as treatment, retaining every per-slot readback/equality and full residency publication check; record per-direction bytes, submission host time, checked wait time, total refill wall time, slot counts, driver faults/resets, completion/error status and exact environment/build/provider identity; (3) only then compare quiet unchanged upstream `bench.sh` OFF/ON with repeated/interleaved samples and output/status gates. Keep H2D and D2H separate and preserve the official controls; do not normalize logical bytes as actual PCIe bytes. Current OFF control is median 384.8 prefill / 7.8 decode tok/s from three 32,049-input/24-output samples; it is not an ON comparison. Do not infer speed from it.

## Source references

Reviewed production source at supplied HEAD: `src/core/gpu.cpp:108-120,244-269,371-382`; `src/core/device.cpp:301-323,326-408,494-531`; `src/core/phase_cache_backend.cpp:110-120`; `src/core/phase_cache_owner.cpp:282-307`; `src/core/expert_cache.cpp:198-228`; `include/strata/core/runtime.hpp` and `include/strata/core/phase_cache_owner.hpp`. Prior allowed compact evidence consulted: R373v2, R375, R377, R360, R362 and committed phase-OFF control report/summary. Registry v189 declares 922 reports; this report was not registered into that chain.

## Primary references

- Intel LLVM/DPC++ [experimental SYCL virtual memory extension](https://github.com/intel/llvm/blob/sycl/sycl/doc/extensions/experimental/sycl_ext_oneapi_virtual_mem.asciidoc#physical-memory-representation): mapped VMM pointers behave as device-USM pointers and may be used with interfaces that accept device USM. Experimental extension wording and exact implementation conformance still matter.
- Khronos [SYCL 2020 specification, explicit memory operations](https://registry.khronos.org/SYCL/specs/sycl-2020/html/sycl-2020.html): `memcpy` endpoints may be host pointers or device-accessible USM pointers; any USM allocation endpoint must share the queue context.
- Khronos [SYCL USM pointer queries](https://github.khronos.org/SYCL_Reference/iface/usm_pointer_queries.html): `get_pointer_type` returns `unknown` for pointers outside a valid USM allocation from the queried context. This is an allocation-query rule, not a denial of the separate VMM extension's API interoperability statement.
- oneAPI [Level Zero memory-copy command](https://oneapi-src.github.io/level-zero-spec/level-zero/latest/core/api/apis/command_list.html#zecommandlistappendmemorycopy): both endpoints must be accessible from the command-list device and memory/list must share context; host/device/shared memory is supported.
- oneAPI [Level Zero VMM programming guide](https://oneapi-src.github.io/level-zero-spec/level-zero/latest/core/PROG.html#reserved-device-allocations): reserved VA must be mapped before use in append operations, with examples using mapped VA in command-list copy/kernel calls.
- Intel [Level Zero Immediate Command Lists guide](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/guide/level-zero-immediate-command-lists.html): first-person vendor technical discussion distinguishes immediate submission from regular-list batching and notes host submission and cross-queue dependency tradeoffs. It provides useful scheduling cautions, not a phase-refill performance estimate.
